rubric.why: Identifies chromatin as the thread-like or network-like material in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Describes chromatin as a fine, thread-like network of DNA and proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing chromatin as thread-like or network-like material.

rubric.why: Distinguishes chromosomes as the condensed, visible structures formed from chromatin.
rubric.description: States that chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes during cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chromosomes as condensed chromatin or as distinct structures formed during cell division.

modelAnswer: Chromatin is a fine, thread-like network of DNA and proteins present in the nucleus, usually when the cell is not dividing.
During cell division, chromatin condenses into distinct, visible chromosomes that carry genes.
